result.title: TRACE: Attribute Execution for Sequential Image Editing
result.summary: Given an image and successive user instructions, sequential image editing should return an updated image that satisfies each new request and preserves earlier requirements that remain active. This lets users develop a result without repeatedly restating or repairing their decisions. The difficulty is that a retrieved image can contain a valid color on an obsolete surface, while the current image may lack the newly requested material. Neither reference selection nor a precise object mask alone specifies how to reconcile attributes occupying the same region. We present TRACE, which separates the continuing attribute from its visual carrier and prioritizes local appearance operations under complete-request checks. Active-goal binding identifies what should persist, carrier selection supplies suitable current or newly generated pixels, and tonal calibration reduces tinting near highlights and shadows. Experiments across frozen editors, independent visual readers, new source images, and complete sequential benchmarks support joint color-material recovery and show how local execution preserves the surrounding scene.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 TRACE 用于顺序图像编辑：把持续生效的属性与其视觉载体分离，用 active-goal binding 判定哪些要求仍需保留、为同一区域选择合适像素载体并做色调校准，在冻结编辑器与顺序编辑基准上验证颜色—材质联合恢复。
AI.relevance_reason: 其“跨轮保持仍生效约束＋完整请求检查＋证据（载体）选择”机制，可能与 LVR 中任务必要信息的延续性状态与视觉证据筛选问题形成类比，但方法停留在像素编辑层面，可迁移性有待核查。
